title: Sewage treatment stages: screens, settling, microbes and polishing
examples: What are the stages of sewage treatment?
What is the difference between primary and secondary treatment?
How do you calculate the BOD load on a treatment plant?

stages.label: Primary settling
stages.note: Heavy solids sink in calm water

explain.say: In the hot summer of 1858 the River Thames smelled so bad that London called it the Great Stink, and Parliament finally paid Joseph Bazalgette to build proper sewers. Today a sewage works cleans that water before it reaches the river. Follow the train on the board, from the incoming sewer to the river.

draw.text: Sewage treatment stages: screens, settling, microbes and polishing

stages.label: Primary settling
stages.note: Heavy solids sink in calm water

explain.say: Start at the left. Screens catch rags and wipes; the grit chamber slows the flow just enough for sand and stones to drop. Now the load: a hundred thousand people each send about two hundred litres and sixty grams of BOD a day. BOD is the oxygen microbes would use eating the dirt. That gives twenty thousand cubic metres a day at three hundred milligrams per litre.

stages.label: Primary settling
stages.note: Heavy solids sink in calm water

explain.say: Next, primary settling, lighting up now. In calm tanks about two thirds of the floating solids sink as sludge and about a third of the BOD goes with them. But much of the dirt is dissolved, like sugar in tea, and cannot sink. Who do you think can remove dissolved food?

stages.label: Primary settling
stages.note: Heavy solids sink in calm water

explain.say: Hungry microbes! In secondary treatment they eat the dissolved organics, then settle out in the clarifier. Look at the bars: three hundred milligrams per litre of BOD, two hundred after primary, and just twenty after secondary. That removes about ninety three percent.

draw.text: Common limit: BOD of 25 mg/L or less in the treated water.

explain.say: Tertiary treatment polishes the water: removing nitrogen and phosphorus that feed algae, and UV light to kill germs. The sludge goes to digesters that make biogas to power the plant. Brilliant work! Challenge: why must the grit chamber come before the pumps and tanks?

stages.label: Primary settling
stages.note: Heavy solids sink in calm water

faq.q: What are the stages of wastewater treatment?
faq.a: Preliminary treatment with screens and grit removal, primary settling, secondary biological treatment with a clarifier, and often tertiary treatment for nutrients and disinfection, plus sludge treatment.
Primary settling tanks remove solids that sink or float, typically around 50 to 70 percent of suspended solids and 25 to 40 percent of the BOD.
Microbes in an aerated tank or on a filter eat the dissolved and fine organic matter, then are settled out in a clarifier. It usually brings BOD down to about 20 milligrams per litre.
Extra treatment after secondary: removing nitrogen and phosphorus, fine filtration and disinfection such as UV, so the water can go to sensitive rivers or be reused.
Sludge is thickened and usually digested without air, which makes biogas for energy. The digested sludge is dewatered and may be used on farmland, burned or landfilled.

facts: The EU Urban Waste Water Treatment Directive of 1991 set a BOD₅ limit of 25 mg/L for treated sewage.
One population equivalent is defined as 60 g of BOD₅ per day.
Joseph Bazalgette's London main drainage system was built after the Great Stink of 1858.

quiz.say: Sewage enters a plant at 300 milligrams per litre of BOD and leaves at 15. What percentage is removed?
quiz.show: Sewage enters at 300 mg/L BOD and leaves at 15 mg/L. Removal?

wrong.1: That is the share left, not the share removed.
wrong.2: That subtracts wrongly; 15 is 5 percent of 300.
